creator: Alexander Terp
description:
One failed command in a profile's `post_install` stops tai from re-baselining the managed files that the other commands changed, so the next install stops on a conflict that isn't one. Profiles now hide failures to avoid that.

`post_install` is a single argv. Profiles chain several commands inside it with `sh -c`. memri's setup is one of them: it writes a block into `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, which tai manages. SPEC.md ("A failed hook does not rebaseline") says tai re-baselines managed files only after the hook succeeds, so when any command in the chain fails, memri's block looks like a hand edit and every later install stops on that conflict. One chain ran `render.rad` before memri, and a non-executable `render.rad` skipped memri as well.

To dodge this, every config repo now hides failures. One Codex post-install script exits 0 and lists what failed; the Claude Code profiles wrap `render.rad` in `{ ... || echo WARNING >&2; }`. A broken approval policy then shows up as one easy-to-miss line in a long install log.

Decided direction (2026-10-13): make `post_install` a list of named steps.

- Each step runs whether or not earlier steps failed.
- tai re-hashes managed files after each step. Changes from a step that succeeded are re-baselined; changes from a step that failed are not. This keeps SPEC.md's carve-out ("a partial edit is a conflict worth surfacing") at the level of the step that made the partial edit, instead of letting it block unrelated steps.
- After the last step, tai prints a summary of failed steps and exits non-zero, as a failed hook does today.

Keep accepting today's single-argv form as one unnamed step, so existing profiles keep working. Update SPEC.md's "Post-Install Hooks" section and the tai skill to match. Each step's timeout is open: one per step, falling back to `post_install_timeout`, is the obvious reading.

The code is `runPostInstallHook` in `cmd/tai/main.go`, `PostInstall` in `internal/profile/resolver.go`, and its validation in `internal/config/parser.go`. Card `let-a-bundle-declare` (bundle-declared steps) builds on this one, so do this first.

(Moved from GitHub issue #13, part 3.)
title: Run post_install as named steps that each succeed or fail on their own
